name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.NonUnitalCStarRepresentation.exists_nonzero_projection_rankOne_map
title: A projection represented by a rank-one operator

content.display_title: A projection represented by a rank-one operator
content.one_sentence_role: Obtains all projection, normalization, image and compactness conditions on the same witnesses.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero complex $C^*$-algebra, with no unit assumed. Let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space and $\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)$ a nonzero irreducible representation representing the unique unitary-equivalence class of nonzero irreducible comparisons. There are $p\in A$ and $e\in H$ such that $$p^*=p=p^2,\qquad p\ne0,\qquad\|e\|=1,\qquad\pi(p)=\theta_{e,e},$$ where $\theta_{e,e}(z)=\langle e,z\rangle e$ and the inner product is linear in its second argument. In particular, this same $\pi(p)$ is compact.
content.assumptions: Separability concerns $H$. No prior faithfulness, simplicity, or unit in $A$ is assumed.
content.conclusion: The chosen algebra projection has a rank-one orthogonal projection as its represented image, and that image is compact.
content.proof_summary: Obtain a scalar-corner projection, use faithfulness to keep its image nonzero, apply the rank-one lemma, and substitute its image equation in compactness.
proof_steps: Apply [A nonzero scalar-corner projection](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/NonUnital/MinimalProjection.lean#L102-L159) to the given singleton $\pi$ and separable $H$. It gives $p^*=p=p^2\ne0$ with $pap\in\mathbb Cp$ for all $a\in A$. Apply [Faithfulness on the original algebra](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/NonUnital/Singleton.lean#L33-L94) to obtain injectivity of the same $\pi$. Therefore $\pi(p)=0$ would imply $p=0$, so $\pi(p)\ne0$.

Apply [A scalar corner has a rank-one represented image](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/NonUnital/RankOneProjection.lean#L46-L62) to this same $p$, its scalar-corner equations and the given irreducible $\pi$. The reason its image has rank one is as follows. The operator $P=\pi(p)$ is a nonzero orthogonal projection. Write $\widehat\pi(\lambda,a)=\lambda I+\pi(a)$ on $\widetilde A=\mathbb C\oplus A$. If $pap=cp$, then $$P\widehat\pi(\lambda,a)P=\lambda P+\pi(pap)=(\lambda+c)P.$$ Choose a nonzero $v$ in the range of $P$. Then $Pv=v$, so $P\widehat\pi(\lambda,a)v=(\lambda+c)v$. The unitized representation is irreducible, hence the orbit of $v$ is dense. Its image under $P$ lies in the closed one-dimensional subspace $\mathbb Cv$; continuity therefore gives $P(H)\subseteq\mathbb Cv$. The reverse inclusion follows from $Pv=v$. For $e=v/\|v\|$, the operator $P$ is thus the orthogonal projection onto $\mathbb Ce$, namely $$\|e\|=1,\qquad\pi(p)z=\langle e,z\rangle e\quad(z\in H).$$

The operator $\theta_{e,e}:z\mapsto\langle e,z\rangle e$ is bounded and has one-dimensional range, so it is compact: the closure of the image of the unit ball is a closed bounded subset of the finite-dimensional space $\mathbb Ce$. Substituting $\pi(p)=\theta_{e,e}$ gives compactness of the same $\pi(p)$. This does not assert that the entire subspace $\mathbb Ce$ is a compact set. The same $p$ therefore satisfies all the stated clauses.
lean_realization_notes: The proof obtains a scalar-corner projection, but minimality is not a separate field in the displayed conclusion.
